source_rule: Every pet rule and official URL was checked on an official park or campground page. No rule or URL was invented. Photos are Wikimedia Commons files with a verified CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, or Public Domain license.

spots.name: Acadia National Park
spots.quality_sentence: One of the few U.S. national parks that welcomes leashed pets on about 100 miles of hiking trails and 45 miles of carriage roads, with three developed campgrounds on Mount Desert Island and the Schoodic Peninsula.
spots.pet_rule: Pets must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet (2 m) at all times and may not be left unattended, including at campsites or in cars. Pets are permitted at Blackwoods, Seawall, and Schoodic Woods campgrounds and on most hiking trails and carriage roads, but not on ladder-and-rung routes, at Sand Beach (June 15–September 8) or Echo Lake (May 15–September 15), or in lakes used as public water supplies.

spots.name: Shenandoah National Park
spots.quality_sentence: A long Blue Ridge park along Skyline Drive, and one of the few U.S. national parks that allow leashed pets on trails — more than 500 miles of path, minus a short published list of closed routes — plus campgrounds and some pet-friendly lodging.
spots.pet_rule: Pets must be on a physical leash no longer than 6 feet at all times, and waste must be bagged and packed to a trash can. Pets are allowed in campgrounds and on most trails, but are prohibited on a published list that includes Fox Hollow, Stony Man (blue-blazed summit spur), Limberlost, Dark Hollow Falls, Story of the Forest, Bearfence Mountain, Frazier Discovery, and the Old Rag ridge/saddle/access trails — fewer than 20 miles of the park’s 500-plus miles of trail.
spots.photo_credit: G. Edward Johnson / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Naked_Creek_Overlook_looking_west_Shenandoah_National_Park_VA_2022-06-19_10-00-20.jpg

spots.name: Cuyahoga Valley National Park
spots.quality_sentence: A river-valley park between Cleveland and Akron where leashed pets are welcome on more than 100 miles of hiking trails and on the multi-use Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath Trail.
spots.pet_rule: The park defines pets as dogs, cats, or any animal that has been domesticated. Pets must be on a leash 6 feet or shorter on all park lands at all times, may not be left unattended, and waste must go in a trash can. Only service animals are allowed in park buildings and on the Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad. Pets and service animals are not allowed on the East Rim mountain bike trails, and pets are prohibited at Virginia Kendall Hills during sledding.

spots.name: Congaree National Park
spots.quality_sentence: A floodplain old-growth forest park that welcomes leashed pets on every trail, including the elevated Boardwalk Trail, and in the campgrounds beneath a high cypress-and-hardwood canopy.
spots.pet_rule: All pets must be on a leash 6 feet long maximum and under control at all times, may not be left unattended, and waste must be packed out (bags are available at the visitor center). Pets are allowed on all trails, including the boardwalk, and in the campgrounds.

spots.name: Petrified Forest National Park
spots.quality_sentence: A Painted Desert park that is unusually open to pets: leashed animals are allowed on any paved road or trail and in all designated wilderness, with a fenced dog park beside the Painted Desert Visitor Center.
spots.pet_rule: Pets of all types are welcome. Keep pets on a leash six feet or less in length; do not leave them unattended in a vehicle. Pets are allowed on any paved road or trail and in all designated wilderness. Only service animals are allowed in park buildings.

spots.name: Custer State Park
spots.quality_sentence: A 71,000-acre Black Hills wildlife preserve with scenic drives, lakes, and developed campgrounds, where leashed pets can travel the park so long as they stay off designated swim beaches and out of park buildings.
spots.pet_rule: Pets must be on a leash no longer than 10 feet, may not be left unattended, and are not allowed in any park buildings or on designated swim beaches; clean up after your pet. South Dakota GFP also states that dogs and cats are allowed in pet-designated lodges, cabins, and suites with a pet accommodation fee.

spots.name: Palo Duro Canyon State Park
spots.quality_sentence: Texas’s largest state park, a colorful canyon of the Prairie Dog Town Fork of the Red River, with campgrounds and hiking routes — including the popular Lighthouse Trail — open to leashed pets.
spots.pet_rule: Texas State Parks require pets to be on a leash no longer than 6 feet (or in a car or crate) at all times, never left unattended, and cleaned up after. Pets are not allowed in any park buildings or in or around a designated swim area; proof of a current rabies vaccination must be carried.

spots.name: Valley of Fire State Park
spots.quality_sentence: Nevada’s oldest state park, a landscape of red Aztec sandstone formations northeast of Las Vegas, with designated campgrounds and trails where leashed pets are welcome except inside the visitor center.
spots.pet_rule: Pets are welcome but must be kept on a leash of not more than six feet in length. Pets are not allowed in the Visitor Center. Camp only in designated campground sites. Note: the park has published a temporary full closure to all visitors each year from December 1 through December 14 for maintenance.

spots.name: Deception Pass State Park
spots.quality_sentence: A dramatic saltwater park on Whidbey and Fidalgo islands, known for its high bridge, forests, and beaches, where leashed dogs are an official park amenity on trails and in campgrounds.
spots.pet_rule: Washington State Parks allow pets in most parks, under physical control and on a leash no more than eight feet; owners must clean up, and pets are not permitted on designated swim beaches. At Deception Pass, dogs are allowed on leash; pets are not allowed in the Kukutali Preserve (including Flagstaff Point) or in the tide-pool areas.

spots.name: Watchman Campground
spots.quality_sentence: The main developed campground just inside Zion’s south entrance, with many sites near the North Fork of the Virgin River and a short walk to the visitor center and the park’s only pet-friendly trail.
spots.pet_rule: Properly restrained pets are welcome in developed campgrounds and picnic areas, along public roads and parking areas, and on the grounds of Zion Lodge. Pets must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet (retractable leashes that extend farther are not allowed). The only trail that allows pets is the paved Pa’rus Trail. Pets may not be left unattended in vehicles when heat poses a risk; in campgrounds they may be left restrained only when conditions are safe and the animal is not making unreasonable noise.

spots.name: Mather Campground
spots.quality_sentence: The South Rim’s large pine-shaded campground in Grand Canyon Village, a practical overnight base where leashed pets are allowed in the campground and on trails above the rim — but not below it.
spots.pet_rule: Leashed pets (up to a 6-foot leash) are allowed on South Rim trails above the canyon rim, in Mather Campground, Desert View Campground, Trailer Village, and throughout developed areas. Pets are not allowed below the canyon rim or on park shuttle buses, and may not be left tied or unattended outside or in a vehicle. A kennel at the South Rim accepts dogs and cats only, with proof of up-to-date vaccinations.

spots.name: Greenbelt Park Campground
spots.quality_sentence: A 172-site National Park Service campground in a wooded park just outside Washington, D.C., with showers, restrooms, and about 9 miles of trails where leashed pets are welcome almost everywhere.
spots.pet_rule: Pets are welcome throughout Greenbelt Park except inside the ranger station. When not in a carrier or crate, a pet must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet and under control; do not leave pets unattended in a vehicle or tied to signs, posts, gates, or bike racks. Bag waste and place it in a trash can.
spots.photo_credit: Ben Jacobson (Kranar Drogin) / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Greenbelt_Park,_Greenbelt,_Maryland_001.JPG

spots.name: Banff National Park
spots.quality_sentence: Canada’s flagship Rocky Mountain park, with turquoise lakes, town-adjacent campgrounds, and many day trails — provided dogs stay leashed and you check which routes currently allow them.
spots.pet_rule: Parks Canada requires dogs to be on a leash of 3 metres or less and under physical control at all times in its protected places. In Banff, dogs must stay leashed; never leave a pet unattended in a vehicle, on a campsite, in a tent, or elsewhere; pick up and bin waste; store pet dishes; and note that dogs are not allowed on some trails — check the official Banff trails page and bulletins before you go.

spots.name: Jasper National Park
spots.quality_sentence: A vast Canadian Rockies park of icefields, lakes, and valley campgrounds, where domestic animals may join day outings if they stay under physical control and off posted restricted trails.
spots.pet_rule: All domestic animals must be kept under physical control (on a leash or in suitable confinement) and must not become a nuisance. Parks Canada requires a leash of 3 metres or less in its protected places. Pets may not be left unattended on campsites or in vehicles, may not chase wildlife, and are not allowed in some areas — check notices at trailheads and information centres. Clean up after your pet. Dogs are not permitted on trails with seasonal restrictions.

spots.name: Cape Breton Highlands National Park
spots.quality_sentence: A highland and coastal park on the Cabot Trail, with spruce plateaus, sea cliffs, and developed campgrounds, where leashed pets are welcome on most routes except the Skyline Trail and certain beaches.
spots.pet_rule: Pets must be kept on a leash at all times and droppings must be picked up. Parks Canada also requires a leash of 3 metres or less in its protected places. No pets are allowed on the Skyline Trail or in certain beach areas; comply with signage.

spots.name: Fundy National Park
spots.quality_sentence: A Bay of Fundy coastal park of Acadian forest, waterfalls, and several developed campgrounds, where leashed pets may join you at picnic areas, campsites, and along many trails.
spots.pet_rule: Pets must be kept on a leash at all times and are never to be left unattended. Parks Canada also requires a leash of 3 metres or less in its protected places. You may have your dog at picnic areas, camping areas, and along many trails. Dogs are not allowed in washrooms or cooking shelters; campground rules also bar pets from kitchen shelters and washrooms, Bennett Lake beach, the swimming pool, and the golf course. Clean up after your dog.

spots.name: Algonquin Provincial Park
spots.quality_sentence: Ontario’s classic canoe-country park on the Highway 60 corridor, with lakeside campgrounds and many hiking trails where leashed domestic animals are welcome except on Mizzy Lake Trail, beaches, and posted pet-free loops.
spots.pet_rule: Your pet must be under control and on a leash not exceeding 2 metres (6 feet) at all times. Official park rules treat this as a domestic-animal requirement. Pets are not permitted in swimming areas, on beaches, or in posted prohibited areas. Dogs are not permitted on Mizzy Lake Trail. Some campground loops are pet-free (Achray sites 20–39, Canisbay 53–101, Mew Lake 95–131, Pog Lake 201–231). Do not leave dogs unattended; pick up waste.

spots.name: Wells Gray Provincial Park
spots.quality_sentence: A large interior-British Columbia wilderness of volcanoes, lakes, and waterfalls — including Helmcken Falls — where dogs and other pets are welcome in the road-accessible frontcountry if they stay leashed.
spots.pet_rule: Dogs and other pets are welcome but must be leashed in the frontcountry (any area within 1 km of a highway or park road). Pets are not allowed in beach areas or most park buildings; dispose of waste in the bins provided. In the backcountry (more than 1 km from a road), dogs may be off leash, though BC Parks warns of bears and other wildlife; some sub-areas such as Trophy Mountain ask that dogs, if brought, stay leashed and on the trail.

spots.name: Killarney Provincial Park
spots.quality_sentence: A Georgian Bay park of white quartzite ridges and clear lakes such as George Lake, where Ontario Parks rules welcome leashed domestic animals on campsites, park roads, and most hiking trails.
spots.pet_rule: Killarney’s official park rules require a domestic animal to be under control and on a leash not exceeding 2 metres at all times. Pets are not permitted in the swimming area, on the beach, or in a posted prohibited area. Ontario Parks also requires that dogs not be left unattended and that waste be picked up. No Killarney-specific dog-free hiking trail was listed on the park’s official activities page at the time of verification; still check posted signs on arrival.

spots.name: Lake of Two Rivers Campground
spots.quality_sentence: A popular Highway 60 campground on a broad Algonquin lake, with forested sites close to the water — a classic road-trip overnight, provided pets stay off the beach and swimming area.
spots.pet_rule: The campground’s official rules require your pet to be under control and on a leash not exceeding 2 metres at all times (a domestic-animal rule). Pets are not permitted in the swimming area, on the beach, or in a posted prohibited area. Lake of Two Rivers is not among the Algonquin loops listed as pet-free on the official Ontario Parks dogs page. Do not leave pets unattended; pick up waste.
